All 6 tests pass now. Two bugs were fixed in `lrucache/cache.py`, both in the LRU ordering logic:

1. **`get` didn't refresh recency** (`cache.py:30`): a cache hit returned the value without calling `move_to_end`, so reads never counted as "use". In the failing test, reading `"a"` should have made `"b"` the eviction candidate, but `"a"` got evicted instead. Fixed by moving the key to the most-recently-used end on every successful `get`.

2. **`put` evicted on in-place updates** (`cache.py:33`): the eviction check was just `len >= capacity`, so overwriting an existing key at capacity still popped the LRU entry even though the cache wasn't growing. Fixed by only evicting when the key isn't already present.

`SOLUTION.md` documents both root causes, and no test files were touched.

Done — `python3 -m pytest -q` passes all 6 tests. Both bugs were in `lrucache/cache.py`:

1. **`get()` didn't refresh recency.** A cache hit returned the value without `move_to_end`, so reads never counted as "use" and a freshly-read key could still be evicted as least-recently-used. Fixed by moving the key to the end of the `OrderedDict` on every non-expired hit (`cache.py:30`).

2. **`put()` evicted on in-place updates.** It evicted whenever the cache was at capacity, even when the key being written already existed, so overwriting a key in a full cache wrongly dropped an unrelated entry. Fixed by evicting only when the key is new (`cache.py:34`).

`SOLUTION.md` at the repo root explains both root causes. No test files were touched and no commits were made.

Done — all 6 tests pass. There were two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`:

1. **`get` didn't refresh recency** (`cache.py:30`): a hit returned the value without moving the key to the most-recently-used end of the `OrderedDict`, so recently-read entries could still be evicted first. Fixed by calling `move_to_end(key)` on every valid hit.

2. **`put` evicted on in-place updates** (`cache.py:33`): the eviction check only looked at size, so overwriting an existing key in a full cache wrongly evicted the LRU entry. Fixed by evicting only when the key isn't already present, since updating an existing key doesn't grow the cache.

Both fixes are explained in `SOLUTION.md`, and `python3 -m pytest -q` reports `6 passed`.

Both bugs are fixed and the full suite passes (`6 passed`). Summary:

**Bug 1 — `get` didn't refresh recency.** It returned the value without promoting the key, so a `get` didn't count as a "use" (contrary to the docstring). A later full-capacity `put` then evicted the just-read key instead of the actual LRU entry. Fixed by adding `self._data.move_to_end(key)` before returning.

**Bug 2 — `put` evicted on in-place updates.** Eviction fired on `len >= capacity` even when the key already existed, so updating an existing key at full capacity dropped an unrelated entry. Fixed by only evicting when the key is new (`key not in self._data and ...`).

The tests directory was left untouched, no commits were made, and I wrote `SOLUTION.md` documenting the root causes.

I fixed two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`:

1. **`get` didn't refresh recency** — despite the docstring saying both `get` and `put` count as a "use", `get` never moved the accessed key to the most-recently-used end. Added `self._data.move_to_end(key)` on a successful read.

2. **`put` evicted on in-place updates** — the eviction check ran unconditionally, so updating an already-present key at full capacity would evict an innocent entry even though the entry count wasn't growing. Now it only evicts when the key is new (`key not in self._data`).

I also wrote `SOLUTION.md` explaining both root causes. I did not touch anything under `tests/` and made no git commits.

Both bugs are fixed and the full suite passes (6 passed). Summary:

**`lrucache/cache.py`** had two LRU-correctness bugs:

1. **`get` never refreshed recency** — it returned the value without `move_to_end`, so a read key stayed marked least-recently-used and got evicted on the next `put`. Fixed by adding `self._data.move_to_end(key)` before returning.

2. **`put` evicted on in-place updates** — the eviction guard was `len(self._data) >= self.capacity`, which triggered even when updating an existing key, wrongly popping the LRU entry at full capacity. Fixed by guarding with `key not in self._data and ...`.

I also wrote `SOLUTION.md` explaining both root causes. The tests under `tests/` were left untouched, and no commits were made.

`make test` now exits 0 — the check script runs (`config ok`, `all checks passed`) and all 3 pytest tests pass. There were four separate environment/config problems from the merge, documented in `SOLUTION.md`:

1. **Makefile recipe indented with spaces** (line 4) — make requires a tab, so it died with `missing separator`. Replaced the spaces with a tab.
2. **`scripts/run_checks.sh` lost its executable bit** — `Permission denied`. Restored with `chmod +x`.
3. **`scripts/run_checks.sh` had CRLF line endings** — the shebang resolved to `/bin/bash\r`, producing the misleading `No such file or directory`. Converted to LF.
4. **Trailing comma in `data/config.json`** — invalid JSON, so `tools/validate_config.py` failed. Removed the comma after `"batch_size": 500`.

No files under `tests/` were touched, no Python source was modified, and the Makefile still runs the identical `check` target and full test suite.

`make test` now passes (exit 0). I diagnosed and fixed three environment/config problems from the botched merge, without modifying anything under `tests/` or weakening any check — the same `check` target and the same pytest suite still run.

**The three problems:**

1. **Makefile line 4 indented with spaces, not a tab** → `missing separator. Stop.` (nothing ran). Restored the tab.
